verses.zh: 扫罗的儿子伊施波设听见押尼珥死在希伯仑，手就发软；以色列众人也都惊惶。
verses.en: When Ish Bosheth[NOTE:1] the son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, he was very disheartened,[NOTE:2] and all Israel was afraid.
notes: The MT does not specify the subject of the verb here, but the reference is to Ish Bosheth, so the name has been supplied in the translation for clarity. 4QSama and the LXX mistakenly read “Mephibosheth.”
Heb “his hands went slack.”
verses.commentary:
4:1 Ish-bosheth was a weak and fearful king (cf. 2 Sam. 3:11). The MT does not have the name, only the
designation, "son of Saul." His name was Ish-baal, see full note at 2 Sam. 2:8.

There are two surprising things about this verse.

- the LXX and DSS have "Mephibosheth," not "Ish-bosheth"

- the plural is surprising, referring to the king

▣

NASB
"he lost courage"

NKJV, JPSOA
"he lost heart"

NRSV, REB
"his courage failed"

TEV
"he was afraid"

NJB
"his heart failed him"

LXX
"his hands were weakened"

Peshitta
"he trembled"

The MT has "they dropped their hands." This is a common OT idiom for loss of control/power/ability to act.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

verses.zh: 扫罗的儿子伊施波设有两个军长，一名巴拿，一名利甲，是便雅悯支派、比录人临门的儿子。比录也属便雅悯。
verses.en: Now Saul’s son[NOTE:1] had two men who were in charge of raiding units; one was named Baanah and the other Recab. They were sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, who was a Benjaminite. (Beeroth is regarded as belonging to Benjamin,
notes: The present translation, “Saul’s son had two men,” is based on the reading “to the son of Saul,” rather than the MT’s “the son of Saul.” The context requires the preposition to indicate the family relationship.
verses.commentary:
4:2 The two brothers who will kill Ish-bosheth were raiding party leaders.

- Baanah

- Rachab

A raiding party is mentioned in 2 Sam. 3:22.

▣ The parenthesis in vv. 2b-3 is an editorial note explaining the people group called Beerothites.
These brothers were either Israelites of the tribe of Benjamin or non-Israelites living in Benjamin's territory.

The phrase "until this day" is a textual marker of a later editor.

verses.zh: 比录人早先逃到基他音，在那里寄居，直到今日。
verses.en: for the Beerothites fled to Gittaim and have remained there as resident foreigners until the present time.)[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “until this day.”

verses.zh: 扫罗的儿子约拿单有一个儿子名叫米非波设，是瘸腿的。扫罗和约拿单死亡的消息从耶斯列传到的时候，他才五岁。他乳母抱着他逃跑；因为跑得太急，孩子掉在地上，腿就瘸了。
verses.en: Now Saul’s son Jonathan had a son who was crippled in both feet. He was five years old when the news about Saul and Jonathan arrived from Jezreel. His nurse picked him up and fled, but in her haste to get away, he fell and was injured.[NOTE:1] Mephibosheth was his name.
notes: Heb “and was lame.”
verses.commentary:
4:4 This verse informs us that there was yet a descendant of Saul's family, a crippled son of Jonathan. His
name was "Meri-baal." Like Ish-baal, later editors changed the name to Mephibosheth. Bosheth means "shame."
These later editors were offended by the name Ba'al, which became the Canaanite name "lord" and referred to the
male fertility god of the Canaanite pantheon.

The UBS Text Project, p. 215, gives "Mephibaal" a "B" rating (some doubt).

- Meri-baal ‒ מריבעל (cf. 1 Chr. 8:34; 9:40)

- Mephibaal ‒ מפיבעל

- Mephibosheth ‒ מפיבשׁת

See full note at 2 Sam. 2:8.

The fact that Jonathan's son was lame made him unacceptable as king. There was no rival to David
becoming king. David was very kind to Jonathan' son (cf. 2 Samuel 9).

verses.zh: 一日，比录人临门的两个儿子利甲和巴拿出去，约在午热的时候到了伊施波设的家；伊施波设正睡午觉。
verses.en: Now the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite—Recab and Baanah—went at the hottest part of the day to the home of Ish Bosheth, as he was enjoying his midday rest.
verses.commentary:
4:5-8 There seem to be two accounts of Ish-bosheth's death put side by side.

- they struck him in the belly on his bed

- they struck him and beheaded him on his bed (this is missing in Peshitta and Vulgate)

The Jewish Study Bible, p. 626, suggests that v. 6 may be corrupt because the LXX is so different and
that v. 7 follows v. 5 so easily.

verses.zh: 他们进了房子，假作要取麦子，就刺透伊施波设的肚腹，逃跑了。
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] entered the house under the pretense of getting wheat[NOTE:2] and mortally wounded him[NOTE:3] in the stomach. Then Recab and his brother Baanah escaped.
notes: For the MT’s וְהֵנָּה (vehennah, “and they,” feminine) read וְהִנֵּה (vehinneh, “and behold”). See the LXX, Syriac Peshitta, and Targum.

Heb “taking wheat.” The reference to getting wheat is obscure and traditionally inferred to mean that they came under the pretense of obtaining wheat (KJV, ESV, NASB, NIV, HCSB). However the plausibility of this scenario is not culturally certain.tc The LXX (followed by NLT) reads, “behold the house doorkeeper was cleaning wheat and became drowsy and fell asleep and the brothers Rekcha and Baana avoided notice.” Josephus refers to the LXX with a slight expansion on the tradition in Ant. 7:48. The last sentence appears to follow the Hebrew MT, although understanding the final verb נִמְלָטוּ (nimlatu; Niphal of מָלַט, malat) “to escape” as “escaping notice” is without parallel. The beginning of the verse in the LXX shares at least the words “midst of house” and “wheat” with the Hebrew MT. What sort of textual corruption through common scribal copying errors could lead to the different texts is unclear.
Heb “and they struck him down.”
verses.commentary:
4:6 The LXX has a very different form of this verse.

"And behold, the porter of the house was cleaning wheat, and he slumbered and slept, and Rechab
and Baanah, the brothers, escaped notice."

verses.zh: 他们进房子的时候，伊施波设正在卧房里躺在床上，他们将他杀死，割了他的首级，拿着首级在亚拉巴走了一夜，
verses.en: They had entered[NOTE:1] the house while Ish Bosheth[NOTE:2] was resting on his bed in his bedroom. They mortally wounded him[NOTE:3] and then cut off his head.[NOTE:4] Taking his head,[NOTE:5] they traveled on the way of the rift valley[NOTE:6] all that night.
notes: After the concluding disjunctive clause at the end of v. 6, the author now begins a more detailed account of the murder and its aftermath.
Heb “he”; the referent (Ish Bosheth) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “they struck him down and killed him.” The expression is a verbal hendiadys.
Heb “and they removed his head.” The Syriac Peshitta and Vulgate lack these words.
The Lucianic Greek recension lacks the words “his head.”
The rift valley is a large geographic feature extending form Galilee to the gulf of Aqaba. The portion in view here runs along the west of the Dead Sea.

verses.zh: 将伊施波设的首级拿到希伯仑见大卫王，说：「王的仇敌扫罗曾寻索王的性命。看哪，这是他儿子伊施波设的首级；耶和华今日为我主我王在扫罗和他后裔的身上报了仇。」
verses.en: They brought the head of Ish Bosheth to David in Hebron, saying to the king, “Look! The head of Ish Bosheth son of Saul, your enemy who sought your life! The Lord has granted vengeance to my lord the king this day against[NOTE:1] Saul and his descendants!”
notes: Heb “from.”
verses.commentary:
4:8 The head of Ish-bosheth was

- a way to show disrespect (i.e., Saul beheaded by the Philistines)

- a way to prove they had killed him

verses.zh: 大卫对比录人临门的儿子利甲和他兄弟巴拿说：「我指着救我性命脱离一切苦难、永生的耶和华起誓：
verses.en: David replied to Recab and his brother Baanah, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, “As surely as the Lord lives, who has delivered my life from all adversity,
verses.commentary:
4:9 David swears an oath by the name of YHWH ("as the Lord lives," cf.
1 Sam. 14:39). He characterizes YHWH as the one who "redeemed his life from all enemies." Thus implying he
did not need the help of these two brothers to deal with his former enemy's family.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

verses.zh: 从前有人报告我说，扫罗死了，他自以为报好消息；我就拿住他，将他杀在洗革拉，这就作了他报消息的赏赐。
verses.en: when someone told me that Saul was dead—even though he thought he was bringing good news[NOTE:1]—I seized him and killed him in Ziklag. That was the good news I gave to him!
notes: Heb “and he was like a bearer of good news in his eyes.”
verses.commentary:
4:10 These two brothers obviously had not heard, or at least understood, what David did to the Amalekites in
2 Samuel 1 who claimed to have killed Saul.

verses.zh: 何况恶人将义人杀在他的床上，我岂不向你们讨流他血的罪、从世上除灭你们呢？」
verses.en: Surely when wicked men have killed an innocent man as he slept[NOTE:1] in his own house, should I not now require his blood from your hands and remove[NOTE:2] you from the earth?”
notes: Heb “on his bed.”
See HALOT 146 s.v. II בער. Some derive the verb from a homonym meaning “to burn; to consume.”
verses.commentary:
4:11 David calls these brothers "wicked men." There may be an intentional word play between

- men (ish), BDB 35

- Ish-bosheth, BDB 36

▣

NASB, NRSV, LXX, Peshitta
"destroy"

NKJV
"remove"

TEV
"wipe you off"

NJB, REB, JPSOA
"rid"

The MT has the VERB (BDB 128, KB 145, Piel PERFECT
with waw), which means "burn" or "consume." Fire was often imagery for YHWH's judgment. Here, it denotes the
complete removal as in a burnt offering.

verses.zh: 于是大卫吩咐少年人将他们杀了，砍断他们的手脚，挂在希伯仑的池旁，却将伊施波设的首级葬在希伯仑押尼珥的坟墓里。
verses.en: So David issued orders to the soldiers and they put them to death. Then they cut off their hands and feet and hung them[NOTE:1] near the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish Bosheth[NOTE:2] and buried it in the tomb of Abner[NOTE:3] in Hebron.[NOTE:4]
notes: The antecedent of the pronoun “them” (which is not present in the Hebrew text, but implied) is not entirely clear. Presumably it is the corpses that were hung and not merely the detached hands and feet; cf. NIV “hung the (their NRSV, NLT) bodies”; the alternative is represented by TEV “cut off their hands and feet, which they hung up.”
4QSama mistakenly reads “Mephibosheth” here.
The LXX adds “the son of Ner” by conformity with common phraseology elsewhere.
Some mss of the LXX lack the phrase “in Hebron.”
verses.commentary:
4:12 David not only killed these men but

- cut off their hands

- cut off their feet

- hung them up exposed for all to see (i.e., improper burial)

Josephus, Antiq. 7.2.1, says David tortured these men, cutting off their hands and feet while
they were still alive.

Why was David so harsh with these brothers?

- They killed Israel's king (son of the anointed King Saul) and, therefore, were worthy of disrespect.

- Again David wants to unite all the tribes. This is another sacrilege against Benjamin. As he distances himself
from Abner's murder, so too, Ish-bosheth's. He showed respect by burying the head with Abner.
